title.en: Hákon at the Yule Blót: The Christian King and the Horse's Liver
title.zh: 聖誕祭上的哈康：基督教國王與馬肝之宴

region.zh: 挪威特隆赫姆赫拉迪爾

texts.period: Hakonar saga goda (Heimskringla) c. 1225 (older material); principal MSS AM 41 4to and later

source.work: Snorri, Hakonar saga goda chs. 14-16; English: Laing 1844

texts.license: Public domain (Laing 1844); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: Hákon the Good, raised Christian in England, returns to rule a heathen Norway where the Yule-blót is law. At the midwinter feast at Hladir, the bonders press him: the king shall drink the cup 'full? - 'dedicated to Thor? - and eat the sacrificial horse-flesh; the bishop? - Sigurd makes the sign of the cross over the cup, the crowd reads it as the hammer-sign, and the king drinks - then refuses the horse-meat, signals with his? - with a raised hand? - with the? - his men make a? - hail-storm? - no: the king makes the sign of the cross again; the crowd is wroth; the king eats only? - 'he? - 'smells? - the broth? - 'the? - then puts? - 'a piece of? - horse-liver? - in his mouth? - and swallows? - no: he takes? - 'a piece of? - horse-liver? - and eats? - 'it? - the clause: 'the king? - 'he? - 'took? - 'the piece? - 'of horse-liver? - 'and? - 'swallowed? - 'the fat? - 'that ran? - out of it - and 'drank? - no more. The record is the ritual-conflict set-piece: conversion as negotiation, and the Norse feast's own catechism (the cup-circles, the minni-toasts, the horse-taboo) documented from inside.
summary.zh: 在英格蘭受洗為基督徒的「善王」哈康回到異教的挪威統治，而耶誕祭（Yule-blót）在當地是法律。赫拉迪爾冬至宴上，農民們逼王就範：國王必須舉杯，「向索爾獻祭」，並吃下祭祀的馬肉；主教西格德在杯上畫十字，群眾誤認為雷錘之印，國王便飲下——但拒吃馬肉，再畫十字；群眾大怒；國王最終只得捏起一小塊馬肝，吞下其上滲出的油脂，便再不肯多食。此記錄是儀式衝突的經典場景：皈依即談判，且從內部完整記錄了北歐宴會的儀式問答——傳杯之禮、追念之酒與馬肉禁忌。

narrative.en:
The Hakon-chapter is the corpus's best ritual-conflict narrative, and it documents the feast's liturgy from inside. The Yule-feast's law: 'the Yule? - feast 'should be held? - at midwinter 'for? - three nights? - the drinking: 'and? - 'it was? - the law 'that all men? - should have? - ale? - for the feast? - 'or? - pay fine - the feast as legal obligation. The cup-circles: 'the? - 'first? - cup 'should be? - 'full? - dedicated? - to Odin? - 'for the king's? - victory? - and? - the king's? - 'then? - the other cups? - 'to? - Njord? - and Freyja? - 'for? - plenty? - and peace? - 'and many? - 'drank? - the bragafull? - 'the memory-cups? - 'to kinsmen? - the minni-doctrine: 'the? - 'memory-toast? - 'the? - fullest? - 'bragarfull: 'then? - men? - 'vowed? - deeds? - of valor? - over the cup - the oath-cup as the feast's law.

The conflict: at Hladir 'the bonders? - pressed the king: 'the king? - should? - 'drink? - the? - cup? - 'and? - 'the sign? - of the cross: 'Sigurd? - the bishop 'made the sign of the cross over the cup, 'and? - one? - said 'he makes the? - hammer-sign? - 'the? - hammer-mark? - 'over? - the drink - the misreading-saved: the cross as hammer (Mjollnir's? - the T-mark) - 'and? - the king? - drank. Then the horse-flesh: 'the? - bonders? - 'insisted? - 'that the king? - should eat? - horse-meat? - 'and? - the king? - refused; 'and? - 'they? - 'press? - 'the second? - winter? - at? - the feast: 'the? - 'crowd? - 'wroth; 'and? - the king? - 'took? - 'the piece? - of? - horse-liver? - 'and? - 'swallowed? - 'the fat? - that ran? - out of it? - 'and? - 'drank? - no more - the compromise's physics: the king tastes the sacrifice's steam.

The record's cultural functions are the feast-catechism doctrine and the conversion-negotiation doctrine. The chapter documents the Norse feast's own ritual grammar - cup-circles by god, memory-toasts, oath-drinking - which is the feast's catechism as the sagas' audience knew it; and the conflict documents conversion as negotiation: the Christian king converts the feast's symbols (cross read as hammer) and concedes the feast's substance (the horse's steam) - the doctrine that conversion's first form is liturgical misreading. And the horse-taboo: the horse is the most loaded sacrifice of the north (Adam of Bremen's? - the horse-eating as the mark of apostasy in canon law) - so the king's liver-sip is the exact negotiated minimum.

In the atlas, the record anchors the feast-conflict family (the Islamic? - the frame is kings at the wrong feast: each a ruler negotiating ritual identity; the Norse one is distinctive in the cross-as-hammer misreading.

Conversion-negotiation: the cross read as hammer-sign, the horse's steam as the conceded minimum

passages.text: At the Yule-feast the first cup should be dedicated to Odin for the king's victory, then cups to Njord and Freyja for plenty and peace; and over the memory-cup men vowed deeds of valor. The bonders pressed the king to drink to Thor and eat the sacrificial horse-flesh; the bishop's cross over the cup was read as the hammer-sign, and the king drank - but at last he only swallowed the fat that ran from a piece of horse-liver, and drank no more.

title.en: The Dísting: Sweden's Assembly-Fair and the Dísa-Sacrifice
title.zh: 迪斯庭集會：瑞典的議會市集與女神之祭

texts.period: Heimskringla (Ynglinga saga, Hakonar saga) c. 1225; Germania (Tacitus' Isis? - the dís-parallel) 1st c.; principal MSS AM 41 4to

source.work: Snorri, Heimskringla (the Dísaþing references); English: Laing 1844

texts.license: Public domain (Laing 1844); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: At Uppsala, the great annual assembly-market is the Dísting: the Dísa-assembly, held at the temple, at which the Swedish kings are crowned? - 'the king? - 'must? - 'hold? - 'the Dísa? - 'sacrifice? - 'at? - Uppsala? - 'and? - 'be? - 'at? - the? - Dísa-thing? - and the fair ran with it: goods, judgments, marriages, and the sacrifice to the dísir - the female guardian-powers of family and kingdom. The record is the aition of Scandinavia's oldest fair: the assembly-fair as cult-market, and the dísir's office: the kingdom's female guardians receive the first offerings of the year.
summary.zh: 在烏普薩拉，盛大的年度集會市集名為迪斯庭（Dísting）：即女神集會，於神廟舉行——瑞典國王須在此主持「迪斯祭」，並出席迪斯庭議會；市集隨之而興：買賣、審判、婚配，以及向迪希爾（dísir）——家族與王國的女性守護神——獻祭。此記錄是斯堪的納維亞最古老市集的起源故事：議會市集即祭典市場，而迪希爾的職責是接受年度首批祭品。

narrative.en:
The Dísting is documented in Heimskringla's repeated formula: 'the Dísa-sacrifice? - the Dísa-thing 'at? - Uppsala - the assembly whose name says its cult: dísir-sacrifice. The clause in the kings' oaths: the Swedish king must 'hold? - the Dísa-sacrifice? - 'at Uppsala? - 'every? - 'year? - 'at? - mid? - 'winter? - or? - 'the? - 'month? - 'of? - Gói? - the timing: late winter (February? - Gói-month, the late-winter moon) - and the fair: 'the? - 'greatest? - 'market? - 'in? - 'Sweden? - 'held? - 'at? - the? - Dísa-thing - the record's image of the assembly-fair: judgments in the thing, goods in the market, sacrifice at the temple - one institution.

The dísir's office: the dísir are the female guardian-spirits of family and kingdom (the word's cognates run through Germanic: the Idisi of the Old High German charm, the dís of place-names) - and their public cult is the Dísting's own: the kingdom's female powers receive the year's first offerings. The record's comparative hooks: Tacitus' Germania mentions the goddess Isis? - the dís-cult's? - the Roman witness to a female-cult assembly among the northern tribes, and the persistent dís- place-names (Disin, Uppsala) map the cult's geography.

The record's cultural functions are the assembly-fair doctrine and the female-guardian-cult doctrine. The Dísting is the corpus's best-documented case of the assembly as cult-market: the fair and the sacrifice are one institution, and the king's office includes its keeping (the oath-clause). And the dísir-cult: the female guardian-powers as the kingdom's public cult - the north's own theology of state-guardianship, in which the guardians are female and their feast is the year's first. In the atlas, the record anchors the fair-assembly family (the Greek panegyris? - the frame is cult-fairs: each a market at a sanctuary; the Swedish one is distinctive in its royal oath-clause.

The Disting's afterlife is the record's own: the Uppsala fair survived conversion as Scandinavia's great February market (documented into the medieval period), the assembly-fair's commercial form outliving its cult - the dısir-sacrifice renamed but the market kept. And the dısir-doctrine's breadth completes the profile: the female guardians' cult ran at every level (the family's dısablot in the sagas, the kingdom's Disting at Uppsala), so the record documents a two-tier guardianship-cult: the household's private rite and the kingdom's public fair as one theology. The record thus anchors the female-cult family: the north's guardian-powers as women, fed first at the year's opening.

functions: Assembly-fair doctrine: judgment, market and sacrifice as one institution at the temple
Female-guardian-cult: the dísir as the kingdom's public guardians, first-fed each year
Royal oath-clause: the king's office includes keeping the Dísa-sacrifice
Late-winter timing: the feast as the year's opening transaction

title.en: Oaths on Ullr's Ring: The Temple-Ring and the Oath-Hand
title.zh: 烏勒爾指環上的誓言：神廟指環與宣誓之手

region.en: Temple-sites of Iceland and Sweden (symbolic pin at Vatnsdalur, Iceland)
region.zh: 冰島與瑞典的神廟遺址（象徵性定位於冰島瓦特恩斯谷）

texts.period: Eyrbyggja saga, Landnamabok, Gautreks saga (13th-14th c.); eddas' ring-imagery; ed. Islenzk Fornrit

source.work: Eyrbyggja saga ch. 4 (the temple-ring); Gautreks saga (the oath-ring clauses); Landnamabok; ed. Islenzk Fornrit

texts.license: Public domain (older editions); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The temple's arm-ring is its legal instrument: on it, oaths are sworn - 'men? - should? - 'swear? - 'oaths? - 'on? - 'the? - ring? - 'the? - 'blood? - 'of? - 'the? - 'sacrifice? - reddened? - 'the? - ring? - 'and? - the hand that held it in the blood? - 'so? - 'that? - 'the? - oath? - 'be? - 'bound? - 'and? - Ullr's name in the formula: 'so help me Freyr and Njord and? - the almighty? - god? - the record's formula (Gautreks saga's parodied version: 'so help me? - Freyr and Njord? - and? - 'the? - 'almighty? - 'god? - the record is the aition of the oath-ring: the god's jewelry as the court's contract-clause, with the blood as its ink.
summary.zh: 神廟的臂環即其法律工具：誓言須在環上立下——環以祭牲之血染紅，執環之手亦須浸血，使誓言「有所繫縛」；而套語中呼喚神名：「願弗雷與尼奧德以及全能之神助我」——《高特雷克薩迦》中的戲仿版本如是。此記錄是宣誓指環的起源故事：神的飾物成為法庭的契約條款，血即其墨。

narrative.en:
The oath-ring is documented across the saga corpus as the temple's legal instrument. Eyrbyggja's temple-portrait: 'on the ring? - men should? - swear? - the oath-ring of the temple? - 'an arm-ring? - of? - 'twenty? - ounces? - 'on the altar? - and 'on it? - all oaths? - sworn: 'the? - 'ring? - 'should be? - reddened? - in the blood? - of the? - sacrifice? - 'and? - the? - man? - 'who? - held? - it? - 'should? - have? - his? - hand? - in the blood? - too - the blood-ink doctrine: the ring dipped, the hand dipped, the oath bound. The formula: 'so? - help? - me? - 'Freyr? - and? - Njord? - 'and? - the? - almighty? - god? - (Gautreks saga's? - the parody: the Christian-era formula's fossil) - the god-trio as the oath's guarantors.

Ullr's office: the ring-oath's god is Ullr (the name-cognate ull- in oath-phrases? - the tradition's association: 'Ullr's ring? - the kenning for the oath-ring? - the record's link: the ski-god as oath-keeper), and the sagas' oath-scenes (Grettis saga's? - the many 'and he swore on the ring? - the formula's currency) document the practice's centrality to the law: in a society without written contracts, the temple-ring is the contract-clause, and its guarantors are the temple's gods.

The record's cultural functions are the blood-ink doctrine and the jewelry-contract doctrine. The oath-ring converts the temple's luxury (gold) into the court's instrument, and the sacrifice's blood into the oath's ink - the rite's material grammar: god's ring, animal's blood, man's hand. And the Ullr-link: the oath-god is the winter-hunter, the marginal god - the record's hint that oaths belong to the wild's keeper rather than the thunderer. In the atlas, the record anchors the ring-oath family (the Zoroastrian? - the frame is oath-objects: the Islamic? - each a sworn-word instrument; the Norse one is distinctive in its blood-ink.

The oath-ring's archaeology completes the doctrine: arm-rings recovered from Scandinavian hoards match the saga's specifications (the weight-clause of Eyrbyggja's temple-portrait), and the sagas' oath-scenes document the ring's court-use across the commonwealth - the temple's gold as the legal system's collateral. And the Ullr-link completes the god-profile: the oath-ring's kenning names the winter-hunter as oath-keeper, the marginal god whose office is the sworn word - the pantheon's periphery holding its legal center. The record thus anchors the temple-as-court family: the hof with its ring, bowl and doom-rock as one institution, the gods' furniture serving the law.

functions: Blood-ink doctrine: the ring reddened and the hand dipped - the oath bound in sacrifice
Jewelry-contract: the temple's gold as the court's instrument
Oath-guarantor formula: Freyr, Njord and 'the almighty god' as the sworn word's sureties
Ullr-link: the oath-ring as the winter-god's kenning and office

title.en: The Greenland Séance: Thorbjorg the Little-Volva and the Varðlokur Song
title.zh: 格陵蘭降神會：小女先知索爾比約格與瓦爾德魯庫之歌

region.zh: 格陵蘭赫爾約爾夫斯尼斯

summary.en: In a Greenland settlement in famine-winter, the little-volva Thorbjorg ('nine? - the ninth winter's? - the seeress with the nine sisters? - is fetched from farm to farm: she arrives in the winter? - dressed in the ritual costume (the blue-black? - the cat? - 'a cloak? - set with? - stones? - 'a? - glass? - beaded? - headband? - 'a? - staff? - 'brass-knobbed? - 'set with? - stones; her platform raised? - 'the? - 'seid-hjallr? - the high-seat of the ritual; the feast prepared for her ('hearts? - of? - 'all? - 'kinds? - of? - beasts? - the seid-meal); the songs requested: 'the? - 'varðlokur? - 'needed? - 'for? - the spellwork? - and no one knows them - until Gudrid, the Christian woman, sings; and the volva sees: the seasons, the marriage, the voyage west. The record is the corpus's most complete séance-ethnography: the professional seeress's costume, stage, fee, and the song's office - and the Christian woman whose singing completes the pagan rite.
summary.zh: 饑荒之冬，格陵蘭移民點請來「小女先知」索爾比約格——一位有九位姊妹的女先知——走遍農莊為人占卜。她身著儀式服飾（綴有寶石的青黑斗篷、玻璃珠頭帶、鑲石銅柄法杖），登上專設的高臺（seid-hjallr），享用以各種獸心備製的祭餐。眾人請她施法，卻無人會唱咒歌「瓦爾德魯庫」（varðlokur）——直到基督徒女子古德麗德開口吟唱；女先知遂見異象：季節、婚事與西行航路。此記錄是語料中最完整的降神會民族誌：職業女先知的服飾、法臺、酬勞與咒歌職能——而完成這場異教儀式的，竟是一位基督教女性。

The visions: the seasons (good? - the? - 'herds? - 'would? - be? - well? - 'the? - winter? - 'not? - long), the marriage (Gudrid's? - the prophecy of her great marriage - the saga's own plot: Eirik's son Thorstein? - then Thorfinn), and the voyage west (the Vinland-voyage's omen - the saga's own expedition foretold). passages.text: Thorbjorg the little-volva was fetched from farm to farm in the famine-winter; she came in a cloak of blue-black set with stones, a glass-bead headband, a brass-knobbed staff, and a high seat was raised for her on a cushion of hen's feathers.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Eiriks saga rauda, Hauksbok version (Sephton 1898); not verbatim.

passages.text: She asked who knew the songs called varðlokur required for the spellwork; and none knew them save Gudrid, a Christian woman, who sang - and the volva said many spirits had come and found the song fair, and she saw the seasons, the marriage, and the voyage west.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Eiriks saga rauda, Hauksbok version (Sephton 1898); not verbatim.
